text:
nina: Planning a maintenance for us-west3: Sat 2025-12-06 04:00 UTC. Scope: PDU firmware swap + targeted node soft-reboots on racks r20-r22. Expected impact: brief GPU eviction for ~8% of capacity in 'aurora' pool. Window: 75m.
pete: what's the cohort plan? will we do parallel PDUs or sequential?
nina: sequential per rack, cohorts of 8 nodes. We'll cordon, drain, power-cycle, verify BMC + nvlink health, then uncordon. Target 8 nodes / 4 minutes -> ~64m total + buffer.
alex: please call out KV cache reseed behavior — we've seen cold p99 regressions after previous swaps.
nina: agreed. We'll run a two-step reseed: local kv warm after each rack, then cross-rack prefix-prime for 15m. Also enable traffic-shaping to prefer ember reserve pool for non-critical requests.
morgan: oncall swap: I can cover the start, @alex take the tail?
alex: yep I can. I'll keep an eye on synthetic traces and tail logs.
pete: cost question: how much burst will we consume if ember kicks in? finance needs an estimate.
finance: can you add a rough number now?
nina: rough calc: ~\$900 total (burst + spot) assuming 20% of aurora load bursts over 75m. I'll put precise calc in the incident.
pete: need a short rollback plan if PDU firmware fails mid-swap.
nina: rollback: stop swap, power-stable fallback (use spare PDU on rX), revert firmware state if available, re-route traffic to ember pool, mark racks as degraded and open incident SEV-2. We'll add exact commands to runbook.
morgan: ops runbook snippet:
```bash
# cordon + drain cohort
fleet ops cordon --rack r20 --nodes 8
fleet ops drain --nodes @r20-cohort --grace 240 --stagger 30s
# swap PDU via on-site script (manual step)
./pdu-swap --rack r20 --target pdu-b
# post-swap checks
./healthcheck.sh --rack r20 --check bmc,nvlink,power
```
alex: add a dry-run canary 20m before start to validate healthcheck script and kvseed.
ops-bot: maintenance ticket created INC-2025-489 by nina  scheduled reminders: 3h, 1h, 10m. Customer-facing blurb: "Planned infrastructure maintenance in US-West3; short interruptions possible for GPU jobs."
finance: noted on cost. Please tag the ticket with billing:project-infra-maint.
pete: also block new large batch CUDA jobs 03:30-06:00 UTC.
nina: blocking implemented on the queue. Also toggling routing policy to use quantized-1 variant for background reranks during window for lower memory pressure.
morgan: will notify enterprise tenants and product leads. I'll post final confirm 1h before.
alex: I'll watch p95/p99 for model calls and post a quick summary at +30m.
nina: thanks team. If anything falls over, escalate to oncall list in the runbook (included). Closing note: keep the post-window 30m warmup traffic muted via routing policy to avoid sudden KV churn.
